newsitem.title: LATVIA: Man still tries to buy into Latvian plant.
newsitem.headline: Man still tries to buy into Latvian plant.

text.p: British commodities group E.D.&F Man Plc is still trying to buy into Latvia's Jelgava Sugar Factory but a meeting of the firm's shareholders has again failed to approve the agreement, Riga daily Diena said on Monday.
The newspaper said a new meeting would be held in two weeks' time.
It added that some shareholders were concerned that after the deal the farmers' share in the plant would fall from the current 85 percent.
They were also worried that the price of sugar beet bought by the plant would fall quickly after Man became a shareholder, the newspaper added.
Under the deal, Man would buy 50 percent of the shares of the firm for 1.3 million lats. It would also lend 1.12 million lats to beet growers to help develop the sector.

Man has been involved in the Latvian sugar sector since 1993, when it signed a deal to buy all of the country's sugar output. The deal ended in 1996. This year only two sugar plants, Jelgava and Liepaja, signed a deal with Man.
